column3: Gomoku versus Jev. Teaching a judgment model to play five in a row.
Jev doesn't write text. You give it a situation and typed questions, and it answers with calibrated probabilities.
So the work is split. Code handles the rules and describes the position. Jev makes the judgment: which move, out of every empty point.
Early on, Jev looked weak. Every time, the board description was wrong. Once threats were stated as facts, forced moves went from zero of twelve to twelve of twelve.
Then, a loop. Play twenty games. Replay the losses. Fix one fact. Play again. No engine answers, only truer facts.
Here, Jev plays black, and wins with a four-three.
Long forcing sequences are still beyond it. Come and play Jev.
